identity.retryPolicy: Transport failures (timeout (180s), network error, HTTP 408/409/429/5xx, unreadable API response with 5xx, incomplete or missing output) are retried up to 4 attempts per turn with exponential backoff honoring Retry-After and provider reset headers. Live calls use a 5-second minimum pace, increasing automatically to stay under 80% of a reported token/minute limit, and live episodes cool down by 30 seconds; every attempt and sanitized rate-limit header is recorded. Exhausted HTTP 429 retries interrupt the batch as infrastructure rather than counting as model failure. Invalid model output (unparseable JSON, schema violation, refusal) is not retried or repaired: it is recorded as an invalid response and terminates the episode as unsolved. A valid direction that is visibly blocked is not retried or repaired: it is executed as a blocked move, counts as a wall hit, consumes the turn, and the episode continues.

aiTransport.policy: Provider requests use the shared Vercel AI SDK transport with structured output. SDK retries are disabled; Echo Maze owns every retry, pacing delay, and attempt record.

identity.coordinateSystem: Walker-relative coordinates start at (0,0). A successful move right changes x by +1, left by -1, up by +1, down by -1. A blocked move changes nothing. The Walker never receives absolute maze rows/columns.
identity.hiddenStatePolicy: The prompt receives only the narrow observation DTO (open/blocked directions, corridor sightlines, per-visible-cell open directions and isExit flag, last action/result) plus the current run's conversation. No full maze, no exit coordinates, no seed, no optimal route, no unseen cells, and no spectator state may enter the prompt.

payload.notes: Start (0,0). Initial openings: right corridor extends three cells; down is a side cell/dead end. Follow the long right corridor first.
At (1,0), horizontal corridor. Move right toward the junction visible two cells ahead; keep the down branch at the far end for exploration.
At (3,0), corridor continues right to a junction whose next cell opens down and left. Advance right, then inspect the branch.
At (4,0), the right branch is blocked and the corridor opens down three cells. Explore downward; the first cell also branches left, while the far end branches left.
At (4,-1), the left branch leads through a two-cell corridor toward an unexplored junction, while down is another branch to defer. Explore left first.
At (2,-1), the corridor continues left to a junction one cell away, while up and down are blocked. Continue left to explore the junction.
At (1,-1), the left route is blocked. The right corridor is already explored; take the unexplored downward corridor and continue mapping for the exit.

At the current vertical corridor, the previous move down succeeded. Both up and down remain open, with three cells visible downward and no side branches; continue downward to explore the unvisited route.
At (1,-4), the vertical corridor remains unexplored downward for two cells, ending at a junction with a left branch. Continue down to reach and inspect that junction.
At (1,-5), the vertical corridor continues down one cell to a junction with a left branch. Continue down to reach that junction and explore the new route.
At the bottom junction, up returns along the explored vertical corridor while left is the new branch. Explore left now and continue mapping for the exit.
At (0,-6) after moving left, both up and right are open. Up returns through the explored vertical corridor; take the unexplored right branch to continue mapping toward the exit.
At (1,-6), the right branch has ended and left returns to the previously visited junction. Explore the open upward corridor; it extends four cells and may lead to the exit or a new branch.
At the vertical corridor after returning upward from the bottom branch. The route upward is the only unexplored direction from here in the current traversal; continue toward the junction ahead.
At (1,-5), continue upward along the corridor toward the unexplored junction ahead. Down returns through the mapped lower branches; right and left are blocked.
At (1,-4), continue upward to the junction one cell ahead. It opens right and may reveal an unexplored route; downward returns to mapped branches.
At the junction after moving up. The downward branch has been traversed, so take the right corridor to continue systematic exploration and search for the exit.
At (2,-3), the corridor continues right to a junction one cell ahead; down and up are blocked here. Continue right to inspect the unexplored junction.

At the current junction, up and left appear to lead through previously encountered corridor patterns. Explore the downward corridor, which extends two cells to a left-turn junction and is the best remaining route for systematic search.
Moved down into the vertical corridor. One more step down reaches the visible junction with a left branch; continue down to inspect this unexplored route.
At the lower junction after moving down. Up returns along the explored corridor; left is the only unvisited branch and should be explored for the exit.
At (3,-6), left is blocked. Up and right appear to reconnect with mapped corridors; take the unexplored downward branch to continue searching for the exit.
After moving down, the current cell opens up and right. Up leads to a short dead-end loop, while right reaches a junction with down and left branches; explore right next.
At the current junction after moving right, left returns to the previous cell while down leads through an unexplored two-cell corridor ending at a left branch. Explore downward.
Moved down into the vertical corridor. The next cell below is the visible junction with a left branch, while up returns to the mapped route. Continue down to inspect the unexplored branch.
At the new lower junction, up returns through the explored corridor while left opens a fresh route extending several cells. Explore left to continue systematic search for the exit.

At the new junction after moving left, the left corridor is still unexplored and extends two cells, while up and right appear to reconnect with mapped routes. Continue left to investigate the fresh branch.
At (3,-11), the corridor continues left to one visible cell that branches down, while right returns through the explored route. Continue left to reach and inspect the new downward branch.
At the new junction, left and up are blocked. The right corridor is mapped, while the downward branch leads to a fresh cell that opens up and right. Explore down.
At the newly reached cell after moving down, up returns to the mapped corridor while right is the unexplored branch. Continue right to investigate the fresh route and search for the exit.
At the end of the newly explored branch, the corridor continues right to a cell opening down and left. Continue right to inspect that junction and search for the exit.
At the junction after moving right, left returns along the recently explored corridor while down leads to an unexplored cell with multiple openings. Explore downward first.
At the new cell after moving down, down is blocked. The left corridor extends three cells and ends at an upward/right junction; right is a short branch. Explore left first.
At (3,-14), the left corridor continues two cells toward an unexplored junction, while right returns to the newly mapped branch. Continue left to explore the remaining route.
At the current horizontal corridor, the left route reaches a new junction one cell ahead with a downward branch, while right returns to the mapped area. Continue left to inspect the junction.
At the new junction, left and down are blocked. The right corridor appears to reconnect with recently explored areas, while the upward corridor extends four cells to a branch. Explore upward first.
Moved up into the unexplored vertical corridor. Up remains open for three more cells toward a junction, while down returns to the mapped area; continue upward to inspect the new branch.
Continue upward through the unexplored vertical corridor. Two cells ahead is a junction with a left branch; down returns to the mapped area. Inspect the new junction next.
At the vertical corridor, moving up reaches the visible junction one cell ahead. The junction should open left; continue upward to inspect this unexplored branch.
At the newly reached junction after moving up. Down returns along the explored vertical corridor; left is the fresh branch. Explore left to continue searching for the exit.
Moved left into the junction. The exit is directly one cell down and visible; take the downward route now.
